title: Newspaper headlines: 'Andy U-turns on early release' and 'Hunt on for eclipse glasses'
text:
The Times leads, external on the letter signed by policing leaders to Prime Minister Andy Burnham, to request extra safeguards for the government's prison early release scheme. The paper notes the significance of the letter, which was signed by all 43 chief constables in England and Wales. The Daily Telegraph says, external the letter is "unprecedented", and reveals forces' anger at the possibility that the killers of PC Andrew Harper could walk free under the scheme. The Guardian focuses, external on the warning from the trade union for probation officers, Napo, that the scheme could increase the risk of inmates being released by mistake.

The prime minister has said middle class areas will have to "play their part" and take in more migrants, according to the Daily Mail, external. Its report says the announcement came as small-boat arrivals under Andy Burnham hit 3,000 in his first 22 days in power.

The i Paper warns, external of rising costs for groceries such as bread, broccoli and steak because of the drought conditions hitting much of England and Wales. It says that puts more pressure on food and drink manufacturers, already facing higher prices as a result of the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

A report in the Financial Times, external says car-part makers in China have quietly amassed greater control of Europe's supply chains, leaving the industry wary. According to the paper, Chinese companies have invested in more than 130 European automotive-parts makers since the mid-2000s, in response to growing resistance to its exports.

The actress, Lucy Davis' revelation that she has terminal cancer leads the Daily Mirror, external. Its front page features a picture of Davis alongside her co-stars from The Office. The Sun quotes, external her saying she is "at peace" with the diagnosis.

Shops across the country have reported selling out of protective eyewear, ahead of tonight's solar eclipse, according to the Metro, external. "The Black Wednesday shopping scramble", reads its headline. The paper says in some cases, people queued for hours to get a pair of glasses and still left empty-handed.
